name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund 10-year spread eased to about 145–150bp on 19 Nov, near the 150bp Alert line; Alert unconfirmed
state: French 10-year yields held just below 4.9% on 19 Nov while German 10-year yields rose to 3.40%, a four-week high (Trading Economics), implying a spread of about 145–150bp, down from 156bp on 17 Nov. The spread closed above the 150bp Alert line in most sessions since late Oct, but this run could not confirm a close above it from two outlets, so the Alert is unconfirmed and the level is Watch. No failed G7 auction or emergency central-bank buying was found.
for_you: High French borrowing costs feed through to euro-area lending rates and to funds holding European government bonds. UK gilts and mortgage pricing can move in sympathy with wider bond-market stress.
rubric_hit: Watch: France–Bund ~145–150bp (19 Nov), inside 80–150bp band; Alert line (>150bp) unconfirmed this run

sources.title: Trading Economics — French OAT yields hold below 4.9%

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
